notes.title: Update - Patch 1.0.10
notes.content: [p]Hello riders! [b]Patch 1.0.10[/b] is here. Based on your feedback following the game's release, it improves [b]gameplay[/b], [b]fixes various bugs[/b] and [b]adds PlayStation[/b] [b]controller[/b] support on PC. Thanks again for your feedback, which helps us improve the game every day! 🤘[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171976/74c18d881be87d5ca9fd31bad85a0252cac149ea.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Changelog[/b] [/h3][list][*][p]Fixed the issue where the QR code for the manga was still shown in the options menu.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fixed the issue where selecting the tab icons dots with the mouse when in the option menu (coming from the main menu) would make the "back" button stop working and by pressing ESC it would show the in game menu, locking the player.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with how the component stats bonus is shown in the hexagonal stats chart (the bonus it the one in yellow, activated by having component all of the same design or all of different design). This bonus wouldn't scale visually with the scale shown by the hexagonal chart, now they are scaled accordingly.[/p][/*][*][p]Added SPACE BAR as a "confirm" input (in addition to mouse LMB).[/p][/*][*][p]Added ESC as main "back" input (in addition to RMB, but now it shows the icon for esc in the interfaces).[/p][/*][*][p]Added ESC as main "hold to exit" button (in addition to RMB, but now it shows the icon for esc in the interfaces). Used in situations like skipping short cutscenes or leaving the extra section.[/p][/*][*][p]Now skipping the use/leave workbench cutscene uses the same "hold to exit" button as the rest of similar situations (which is now ESC). Before it only used LMB.[/p][/*][*][p]Inside TABs with hexagonal scrollers (hoverboard components, materials in the crafting tab, customization, designs) now the user can move horizontally and vertically to a different component, material etc. by clicking on it with the mouse LMB (in addition to using WASD).[/p][/*][*][p]The when opening the menu during play will place the mouse at the center of the screen instead of the top left for better usability.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue that prevented unlocking the "Ride with style" achievement, when collecting all the hoverboard styles.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue that didn't show the correct number of max available styles in the customization section of the workbench.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a sound effect for the platform devices (inside mines) that move based on the position of the player on the platform itself.[/p][/*][*][p]Now when doing races a second time after winning once will have the time time added with ring reduced from 20s to 15s.[/p][/*][*][p]In the Lambda mine, the initial one with a cross made of rails at the start and a cart in the middle, it was possible to activate the doors by using the wheels even if the cart wasn't close to the wheels. tags.bug: Fixed the issue where the QR code for the manga was still shown in the options menu.

Fixed the issue where selecting the tab icons dots with the mouse when in the option menu (coming from the main menu) would make the "back" button stop working and by pressing ESC it would show the in game menu, locking the player.

Fixed an issue with how the component stats bonus is shown in the hexagonal stats chart (the bonus it the one in yellow, activated by having component all of the same design or all of different design). This bonus wouldn't scale visually with the scale shown by the hexagonal chart, now they are scaled accordingly.

tags.feature: Added SPACE BAR as a "confirm" input (in addition to mouse LMB).
Added ESC as main "back" input (in addition to RMB, but now it shows the icon for esc in the interfaces).
Added ESC as main "hold to exit" button (in addition to RMB, but now it shows the icon for esc in the interfaces). Used in situations like skipping short cutscenes or leaving the extra section.

tags.bug: Now skipping the use/leave workbench cutscene uses the same "hold to exit" button as the rest of similar situations (which is now ESC). Before it only used LMB.

Inside TABs with hexagonal scrollers (hoverboard components, materials in the crafting tab, customization, designs) now the user can move horizontally and vertically to a different component, material etc. by clicking on it with the mouse LMB (in addition to using WASD).
The when opening the menu during play will place the mouse at the center of the screen instead of the top left for better usability.
Fixed issue that prevented unlocking the "Ride with style" achievement, when collecting all the hoverboard styles.
Fixed issue that didn't show the correct number of max available styles in the customization section of the workbench.

tags.feature: Added a sound effect for the platform devices (inside mines) that move based on the position of the player on the platform itself.

tags.balance_change: Now when doing races a second time after winning once will have the time time added with ring reduced from 20s to 15s.

tags.bug: In the Lambda mine, the initial one with a cross made of rails at the start and a cart in the middle, it was possible to activate the doors by using the wheels even if the cart wasn't close to the wheels. There where also 2 duplicate d4 lasers that have been removed (the only lasers that should be available are the ones generated by pressing the buttons).

tags.feature: We have added direct support for Playstation controller on PC, with the correct icons appearing. This requires Steam input to be disabled to test it.

notes.title: Get ready to customize you Hoverboard! 🛠️
notes.content:
We'd like to introduce you to an important feature of the game: the Hoverboard customization system, and we hope you enjoy it as much as we do!

Have you already started thinking about what your ideal hoverboard will look like? Elegant and minimalist? Colorful and flashy? Something totally out of the ordinary? The choice is yours!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171976/7b684ac53413612a0b91c467c1f9e624ea62cdc1.gif[/img]

[h3][b]What can you customize? 🎨 [/b][/h3]
[list]
    [*][b]Colors:[/b] Choose your own color palette to bring out your personality.
    [*][b]Components:[/b] Collect crafting components to enhance performance and style.
    [*][b]Designs:[/b] Apply designs, lights to make your style unique
    [*][b]Board Types:[/b] Choose from different board shapes, each with its own unique feel.
[/list]
With so many possibilities, every Hoverboard can look and feel completely different. Whether you're into clean lines or chaotic energy, you’ll be able to create something that truly represents your playstyle.

We can’t wait to see your Hoverboards once the demo and the game is out!
Stay tuned, and get ready ride in style across the galaxy! 🪐

notes.title: ⭐ AMA with the devs! ⭐
notes.content:
[h2]Here are the answers to our recent AMA, straight from [i]Star Overdrive[/i]'s lead developer, Tommaso from Caracal Games. He delves into the game's inspirations, mechanics, and even the story behind the manga! 👀
[/h2]

[table noborder=1]

    [tr]

        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171976/8bb02553661863e5f628c5f446f78a04875c332f.jpg[/img][/th]

        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45171976/a64b41d715c7d1fa05a17828b2c76279aebf9ecb.jpg[/img][/th]

    [/tr]
[/table]

[h3][b]Do you think this game could be fun for someone that enjoys exploration from open worlds but has very limited time? 
[/b][/h3]We wanted to make a "short" open world, so to complete the game it will only take 10-15 hours instead of 80-100 like other open worlds. We also designed it to be played in short sections with no problems (20-30 minutes maybe? Depends on the player!)

[h3][b]What were the inspirations behind the game? Personally, it gave me strong [i]Trigun [/i]vibes.[/b]
[/h3]
[i]Trigun[/i], we love it! You know that Bios' hair is the result of some iteration that started from Vash the Stampede? They have a different temper anyway 🙂

We grew up in the '90s, so anime and manga are for sure one of the sources of inspiration, directly or indirectly. The very first concept of [i]Star Overdrive[/i] was born after I saw [i]Eureka Seven[/i], an incredible anime in terms of visuals and style—and they’ve got hoverboards, of course. You can see a lot of that in [i]Star Overdrive[/i], but a major part of the world design is inspired by the work of Roger Dean and Chris Foss, incredible illustrators from the last century.

For the music, of course, Van Halen 😉

[h3][b]What's the framerate on the Steam version?[/b]
[/h3]The performance will depend on the hardware running the game. However, Star Overdrive is a very light game, so even on some older machines you should be able to run it very well!

[h3][b]What's the manga about? Is it background info, or a retelling of the plot? I see it available as DLC. Is that the only way to read it?[/b]
[/h3]The manga is a parallel project that we worked on over the past year. We wanted to go a little deeper into the story, taking advantage of this different medium to better show the main character's emotions.

Volume 0 is 180 pages and follows part of the game’s story, but it goes deeper into certain aspects and includes an entire section dedicated to a key prequel event that’s not in the game (only mentioned).

The manga is available as DLC on the e-shop, or you can buy the physical version on Amazon. It's called "[i]Star Overdrive - Beyond the Stars[/i]". It's written by me (Tommaso) and illustrated by the awesome Alfredo Postiglione (an Italian mangaka).

[h3][b]Star Overdrive features a unique mix of traversal and combat. How did you balance hoverboard mechanics with enemy encounters to keep gameplay fluid?[/b][/h3]
Cebete (the planet where[i] Star Overdrive [/i]is set) was designed like a giant skate/hoverboard park, with traversal speed in mind. On top of that, we added points of interest for platforming, puzzles, and combat (like mines and towers), as well as activities related to hoverboard riding (like time trials and races). 

The space between these points is kept consistent to ensure you can ride for a bit before reaching the next area of interest. The center of the map is denser with points (since you go slower with the hoverboard there), and the outer areas are more spread out (because you move much faster later in the game).

The really tricky part—which I’m very happy with (I’m also the level designer)—was that we were able to communicate effectively (but indirectly) where the player should ride and where they should explore on foot. Our testers during development, and feedback from the demo, confirmed that it seems to be working well.

[h3][b]What inspired the power-combination system in combat? 
[/b][/h3]The power system was by far the most difficult—but also the most rewarding—system to develop.

It started, of course, with inspiration from [i]Breath of the Wild[/i]’s power system. But since [i]Star Overdrive[/i] needed more fast-paced action, we wanted the powers to be more integrated into the combat. You can use powers in combat in [i]BOTW [/i]too, but in [i]Star Overdrive[/i], the combat system is based on using powers. They have cumulative effects, not only based on physics, but also on mathematical interactions.

We built the system so that combining powers with enemies, objects, or even the hoverboard always creates a result. During development, we actually discovered several cool mechanics by accident, like the “slingshot,” where you link an enemy/object/hoverboard to two points and then use the grab to charge and throw. It was so fun that we added it into the main quest!
